title: Working on My First Stylized Platform for My Indie Game - Would Love Some Feedback!
author: Sashamirae17
selftext:
i'm currently developing my own indie game called **Bollum**, a 2.5D physics-based platformer built in Unreal Engine 5.

After spending a lot of time working on the game's movement, gravity, jumping, bouncing, and physics systems, I've finally started exploring the visual side of the project!

🌿 **This is my very first tropical platform prototype, created in Blender!**

The goal is to create a colorful, clean, and stylized world inspired by high-quality 3D animated films.

I'm aiming for vibrant but harmonious colors, soft shapes, lush vegetation, and environments that feel alive and visually appealing.

**This is just an early prototype, not the final design!** There's still a lot to improve, experiment with, and learn along the way.

💬 **I'd Love Your Feedback!**

I'd really appreciate hearing your thoughts and suggestions!

* What do you think of the visual style?
* Would you change anything about the grass, rocks, colors, or proportions?
* Do you have any tips for improving stylized environments in Blender?
* What would you love to see in a physics-based 2.5D platformer?

🎮 **About Bollum**

Bollum is a physics-based platformer focused on satisfying movement, momentum, jumping, bouncing, creative obstacles, and challenging levels.

The project is still in its early stages, but the goal is to gradually transform it into a polished and enjoyable game.

🎥 **Follow the Development on YouTube - Vornum Studios!**

I've also created a YouTube channel where I'm documenting the development of Bollum step by step.

I'm regularly sharing:

🔹 Development progress and new features  
🔹 Bugs and unexpected issues discovered during development  
🔹 How those bugs are investigated and fixed  
🔹 Gameplay mechanics and physics improvements  
🔹 Blender models and visual experiments  
🔹 The journey from early prototypes to the final game

The idea is to share the **real game development process**, including the mistakes, challenges, solutions, and improvements along the way.

❤️ **If you find the project interesting, I'd really appreciate it if you visited my YouTube channel and subscribed!**

Even a small amount of support means a lot and helps motivate me to keep documenting and improving the game.

🎥 **Watch the Bollum Devlogs - Vornum Studios:**

[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EBWYAdl\_Ntc](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EBWYAdl_Ntc)

I'd love to build a small community around Bollum where people can follow the progress, share ideas, give constructive criticism, and potentially influence how the game evolves.
